subject: ela
intro: Choose the single best answer for each question about planning, supporting, and delivering a presentation of claims and findings.

items.prompt:
Maria is giving a presentation. She says: 'Our school should add more water fountains. On hot days, the line at the only fountain stretches down the hall, and many students never get a drink before class.' Which sentence states her claim?
A) Our school should add more water fountains.
B) On hot days, the line at the only fountain stretches down the hall.
C) Many students never get a drink before class.
D) The line stretches down the hall.
items.answer: A) Our school should add more water fountains.

steps: A claim is the main position the speaker wants the audience to accept, not a fact that backs it up.
Option A states a position about what the school should do, so it is the claim.
Options B, C, and D are facts and details that support the claim by describing the problem, so they are evidence, not the claim itself.
solution.answer: A) Our school should add more water fountains.

items.prompt:
A speaker is presenting the claim 'Our class should take a field trip to the science museum.' Which supporting detail does NOT belong because it is off topic?
A) The museum has a new exhibit that matches our unit on weather.
B) Students who visit museums often remember lessons better.
C) My little brother lost his jacket at the zoo last summer.
D) The museum offers free guided tours for school groups.
items.answer: C) My little brother lost his jacket at the zoo last summer.

steps: Every supporting detail should connect to the claim about visiting the science museum.
Options A, B, and D each give a reason the field trip would be worthwhile, so they are pertinent.
Option C is about a brother losing a jacket at the zoo, which has nothing to do with the science museum trip, so it is off topic and should be cut.
solution.answer: C) My little brother lost his jacket at the zoo last summer.

items.prompt:
Here is a description of a presentation: 'Devon stared down at his note cards the whole time and never looked up at the audience. His voice was loud and clear, and everyone could hear him.' Which delivery feature most needs improvement?
A) Volume
B) Pronunciation
C) Eye contact
D) Speaking speed

steps: The description says Devon was loud, clear, and easy to hear, so volume and pronunciation are fine.
It says he stared at his note cards and never looked up, which is a problem with eye contact.
Option C names the correct weak feature. Options A and B describe parts of his delivery that were strong, and speed (D) is never mentioned.

items.prompt:
A student wants to present these four points about starting a school garden:
(1) 'Here is a plan for which classes would plant and water each section.'
(2) 'Our school should start a vegetable garden.'
(3) 'A nearby school grew enough vegetables to share with the whole cafeteria.'
(4) 'Right now our courtyard is empty dirt that no one uses.'
Which order presents the claim and findings most logically?
A) 2, 4, 3, 1
B) 1, 2, 4, 3
C) 3, 1, 2, 4
D) 4, 1, 2, 3

steps: A logical presentation states the claim first, shows the problem, gives evidence it would work, then proposes the plan.
Point 2 is the claim, point 4 describes the current problem, point 3 is evidence that the idea works elsewhere, and point 1 is the plan, giving the order 2, 4, 3, 1.
Option A matches this order. Options B and D place the plan or problem before the claim, and option C buries the claim in the middle, breaking the logical flow from claim to evidence to plan.

items.prompt:
A student is presenting the claim 'Our town library should stay open later on weeknights.' Which choice is the most pertinent and specific supporting detail?
A) Libraries are good places.
B) A librarian reported that twenty students per night are turned away at closing because they are still studying.
C) I really like reading mystery books at the library.
D) The library has been on Oak Street for a long time.
items.answer: B) A librarian reported that twenty students per night are turned away at closing because they are still studying.

steps: Strong support is a relevant, specific fact that comes from a reliable source and directly backs the claim.
Option B gives a sourced, specific number showing demand for later hours, so it is the strongest support.
Option A is a vague opinion, option C is a personal feeling, and option D is a true fact about the library that does not support staying open later, so none of them is pertinent and specific.
solution.answer: B) A librarian reported that twenty students per night are turned away at closing because they are still studying.

items.prompt:
Read this part of a presentation: 'Our school should switch to reusable lunch trays. Last year we threw away about forty thousand foam trays, which filled the dumpsters and cost money to haul away. Foam trays also take centuries to break down in a landfill.' Which sentence states the claim, and which sentences provide the supporting findings?
A) The second sentence is the claim; the others are details.
B) The third sentence is the claim; the others are details.
C) The first sentence is the claim; the second and third provide facts and details that support it.
D) All three sentences are claims.
items.answer: C) The first sentence is the claim; the second and third provide facts and details that support it.

steps: The claim is the position the speaker wants the audience to accept, while findings are the facts and details that back it up.
The first sentence states the position that the school should switch to reusable trays, so it is the claim.

The second and third sentences give a statistic and a fact about foam trays that support that position, making option C correct. Options A and B mistake a supporting fact for the claim, and option D ignores that facts are not claims.
solution.answer: C) The first sentence is the claim; the second and third provide facts and details that support it.

items.prompt:
Read this mini presentation and the note about delivery: 'Our school should add a homework help club after school. Many students struggle to finish assignments alone at home. At a school across town, grades went up after they started a help club. My uncle once coached a basketball team that won a championship. We could meet in the library on Tuesdays and Thursdays with volunteer tutors.' Delivery note: the speaker was loud, clear, and made good eye contact. Which single revision would most improve this presentation?
A) Tell the speaker to talk louder so the back row can hear.
B) Remove the sentence about the uncle's basketball team because it does not support the claim.
C) Add more sentences so the presentation has as many details as possible.
D) Move the claim to the end so it is the last thing the audience hears.
items.answer: B) Remove the sentence about the uncle's basketball team because it does not support the claim.

steps: The presentation is well delivered, so the fix should target the content, not the delivery.
The sentence about the uncle's basketball team is off topic and does not support the claim about a homework help club, so removing it keeps the findings focused, making option B the best revision.

Option A is wrong because the delivery note says the speaker was already loud and clear. Option C wrongly assumes more details always help, when the real problem is an irrelevant one. Option D breaks logical order by burying the claim instead of stating it first.
solution.answer: B) Remove the sentence about the uncle's basketball team because it does not support the claim.

items.prompt:
Two students each gave a presentation arguing 'Our class should plant trees in the park.' Jordan had strong, sourced facts about how trees cool neighborhoods, but he mumbled and stared at the floor, so the back rows could not hear or follow him. Priya spoke loudly, looked at the audience, and pronounced every word clearly, but her only support was 'Trees are pretty and I like them.' Which statement best evaluates the two presentations?
A) Jordan's was fully effective because his facts were correct.
B) Priya's was fully effective because her delivery was excellent.
C) Neither was fully effective: Jordan needs to improve volume and eye contact, and Priya needs stronger, more relevant supporting evidence.
D) Both were equally effective because each did at least one thing well.
items.answer: C) Neither was fully effective: Jordan needs to improve volume and eye contact, and Priya needs stronger, more relevant supporting evidence.

steps: A fully effective presentation needs both strong support and clear delivery, so you must judge content and delivery together.
Jordan had good evidence but weak delivery (mumbling and no eye contact), while Priya had good delivery but only a personal opinion as support, so each is missing one half.
Option C correctly names the gap in each presentation. Options A and B judge only content or only delivery and ignore the other, and option D wrongly treats 'one thing done well' as fully effective.
solution.answer: C) Neither was fully effective: Jordan needs to improve volume and eye contact, and Priya needs stronger, more relevant supporting evidence.
